A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LoongX and L-Mind. All 22 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A.1–A.7, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original image-editing evaluations, ablations, subject-level results, and an editing-type classification experiment using the collected L-Mind data.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experimental results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The CS3 encoder, DGF fusion, diffusion conditioning, and training losses are retained. Revised tensor notation and added signal labels in Figure 3 describe existing operations rather than a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same L-Mind collection of 23,928 samples from 12 participants, covering 35 editing types, and retain the preliminary editing-type classification task. No dataset, population, or test scenario is added.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains OminiControl with text and speech as comparators. Appendix A.3 retains the same noise, text, and neural-input comparisons; comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: The editing and classification splits, preprocessing, five editing metrics, and training and inference settings remain unchanged. Rephrasing the EEG pyramid settings does not report a different configuration.

E4.justification: The modality, EEG-channel, and architecture ablations, editing-category breakdown, sequence-length analysis, and qualitative failure cases are retained. The boxed findings summarize existing analyses.

E5.justification: Tables 1 and 2 report means and 95% confidence intervals over three runs in both versions. No run-count, seed, uncertainty-reporting, or statistical-procedure change is introduced.

E6.justification: The reported tables, result plots, and qualitative examples retain their results. For example, neural-only LoongX still reports CLIP-I 0.6605 and DINO 0.4812, while signals plus speech retain CLIP-T 0.2588 in Table 1.

T1.justification: The equations retain their mathematical operations. Replacing d_m′ with C, already defined as equal, and relabeling embedding dimensions in Equations 5–6 are notation edits. No substantive derivation, assumption, or proof changes.

C1.justification: The unchanged abstract and retained contributions claim multimodal neural-driven editing, the L-Mind dataset, CS3/DGF components, and complementary speech guidance. The rewritten research questions and conclusion preserve this scope.

C2.justification: Sections 5.1–5.5 rephrase existing interpretations of modality complementarity, semantic fidelity, and ambiguous instructions. The detailed limitations concerning population generalization, noise, sensor resolution, and interpretability remain unchanged in Appendix A.5.

D1.justification: Acquisition and preprocessing details, hardware, optimizer settings, FLUX/LoRA information, inference settings, and resource-release policies are retained. The revision adds no substantive implementation or access information.

R1.justification: The same 66 references and related-work positioning are retained. Bibliography pagination changes without adding or removing cited works.

P1.justification: V2 rephrases the research questions, edits method and experimental explanations, shortens the conclusion, adds appendix cross-references, and revises author-contribution footnotes. The overall section and appendix organization remains stable.

P2.justification: Figure 3 gains signal labels, existing takeaways become boxed answers and findings, and several captions and table layouts change. Table 3 moves within the appendix, while Figure 7 moves from beside its discussion to within the references.

improvement.justification: Added diagram labels and boxed takeaways provide modest readability benefits, but reflow places Figure 7 among the references, separating it from its discussion. These limited presentation tradeoffs leave overall quality essentially unchanged; the scientific reasoning, evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations are retained.
